title: Active wildfire detection via satellite imagery and machine learning: an empirical investigation of Australian wildfires
main_finding: SWIR NIR and NDFI support active-fire discrimination in an NSW case study
limitations: Single locality; Landsat revisit limits near-real-time monitoring; abstract does not establish cross-event generalisation
candidate_gap_relevance: Shows an Australian baseline but leaves room for temporal multi-sensor monitoring and reliability analysis

title: Towards a deep-learning-based framework of Sentinel-2 imagery for automated active fire detection
geography: Eastern Australia and western United States
validation: Tests in Australia and United States
main_finding: Automated framework reported about 6 minutes processing for 12000 square kilometres and IoU around 70–72%
limitations: Semi-manual labels; Sentinel-2 revisit/cloud constraints; limited evidence of uncertainty and unseen-event robustness
candidate_gap_relevance: Strong closest Australian/global comparator; motivates cross-region reliability and temporal fusion

title: Real-Time Wildfire Detection Algorithm Based on VIIRS Fire Product and Himawari-8 Data
main_finding: Combines VIIRS reference information with high-frequency Himawari-8 observations for real-time detection
limitations: Machine-learning labels can be labour-intensive or noisy; performance depends on cross-sensor alignment and contextual thresholds
candidate_gap_relevance: Very close prior art; any fusion proposal must add a distinct reliability/generalisation contribution

title: Active Fire Detection Using the Himawari-8 Satellite: Final Project Report
main_finding: Demonstrated an operational Himawari-8 hotspot trial delivering detections to Australian fire agencies
limitations: Technical report rather than peer-reviewed model study; operational constraints and complete validation details require full-text extraction
candidate_gap_relevance: Establishes that basic Himawari monitoring in NSW is not novel; reliability improvements must be explicit

title: An Enhanced Contextual Fire Detection Algorithm for MODIS
validation: Simulation and high-resolution validation across biomes
uncertainty: confidence classes rather than probabilistic calibration
main_finding: Improved sensitivity to smaller/cooler fires and reduced persistent false alarms
limitations: Fixed contextual rules remain sensitive to background conditions and sensor resolution
candidate_gap_relevance: Essential baseline and source of false-alarm taxonomy

title: The New VIIRS 375 m Active Fire Detection Data Product: Algorithm Description and Initial Assessment
main_finding: VIIRS improves sensitivity to smaller and cooler fires compared with coarser products
limitations: Polar-orbit revisit and cloud/smoke obstruction remain; confidence is not end-to-end calibrated probability
candidate_gap_relevance: Provides label/reference product and operational baseline

title: The Collection 6 MODIS active fire detection algorithm and fire products
main_finding: Collection 6 updates a long-running global operational fire product
limitations: One-kilometre-class product and limited daily overpasses miss small or short-lived events
candidate_gap_relevance: Defines an operational baseline and known sensor constraints

title: Remote Wildfire Detection using Multispectral Satellite Imagery and Vision Transformers
main_finding: Vision transformer captures spatial dependencies in multispectral imagery
limitations: Regional scope; operational latency cross-sensor transfer and calibration are not central
candidate_gap_relevance: Shows that use of a transformer alone is not novel

title: Advancements in remote sensing for active fire detection: A review of datasets and methods
main_finding: Highlights multimodal learning spatiotemporal models self-supervision interpretability and data-quality management as open directions
limitations: Review recommendations do not prove that every combination is absent in Australia
candidate_gap_relevance: Primary source for candidate-gap framing and search expansion

title: Rapid Wildfire Hotspot Detection Using Self-Supervised Learning on Temporal Remote Sensing Data
main_finding: Uses self-supervised temporal representations to reduce dependence on labels
limitations: Preprint; European events; calibration and Australian transfer require evaluation
candidate_gap_relevance: Supports studying label efficiency and geographic transfer rather than generic temporal modelling

title: Sen2Fire: A Challenging Benchmark Dataset for Wildfire Detection using Sentinel Data
main_finding: Introduces a wildfire-detection benchmark intended to support model comparison
limitations: Preprint and benchmark distribution may not represent Australian operational conditions
candidate_gap_relevance: Potential external pretraining/benchmark source; must test Australian transfer

title: TS-SatFire: A Multi-Task Satellite Image Time-Series Dataset for Wildfire Detection and Prediction
detection_or_monitoring_target: active fire daily monitoring and next-day fire
main_finding: Unifies active detection daily monitoring and next-day prediction in one temporal dataset
limitations: Preprint; US geography; task definitions and validation require full-text review
candidate_gap_relevance: Useful benchmark for defining monitoring and temporal models; transfer to Australia is open

title: FireCluster: A multi-source satellite active fire data clustering algorithm for comprehensive wildfire event identification
venue: International Journal of Applied Earth Observation and Geoinformation
main_finding: Adaptive multi-source clustering improves event-identification recall over standard clustering
limitations: China-only evaluation; not a learned calibrated detector; published after many earlier fusion systems
candidate_gap_relevance: Shows multi-source fusion itself is no longer novel; Australian evaluation and trustworthy detection need a sharper claim

title: Real-time wildfire detection with semantic explanations
main_finding: Produces concise semantic explanations while processing high-rate event streams
limitations: Not specifically a multi-sensor satellite detector and does not establish calibrated uncertainty
candidate_gap_relevance: Evidence that explanations in detection exist; gap must specify satellite active-fire reliability and geographic transfer

title: Unsupervised Wildfire Detection Using Multispectral MTG-FCI Data: A Feasibility Study
metrics: lead time detection and false alarms
main_finding: Reported earlier alerts than polar overpasses in many synchronised cases with median lead time around 21 minutes
limitations: New sensor and European geography; unsupervised false-alarm control and cross-region transfer remain concerns
candidate_gap_relevance: Supports geostationary temporal advantage and motivates Australian Himawari comparison
